The Duchy of Ledestrov was founded in the year 840 by a group of twenty-six nobles, who crowned the [[Count of Anavaisk]] as the duke of the region of Ledestrov. Aside from several border skirmishes, Ledestrov managed to remain relatively peaceful, and even incorporated several nearby nations into itself through diplomatic means. 

== Historical Overview ==

=== '''Establishing the Elections''' ===
After a series of increasingly ineffective leaders, the noble council, then consisting of thirty-three members, banded together to depose the duke in 1352. The council then chose to elect the [[Prince of Novoanov]], under the condition that a more permanent decision-making body be formed. The signing of the [[Anavaisk-Novoanov Accords]] led to the formation of the Duma, which would be made of all landed nobles owing their allegiance to the duke. A simple majority in the Duma would be required for all declarations of war, budgetary changes, and foreign treaties. A ⅔ majority would be required to elect the next Duke of Ledestrov upon their death. Should a ⅔ majority not be achieved, the eldest child of the previous duke would be appointed as regent, until the Duma could elect a new duke. 

=== '''Revolt and the Pentarchy''' ===
As the duchy evolved and industrialized, both the successive dukes and the people became increasingly frustrated with the nobles of the Duma. While an effective change at first, as the centuries went on, the nobles became increasingly corrupt and self-serving. After a famine in 1938, seven years since the Duma had even managed to pass a budget, the then Duke of Ledestrov, the [[Burgrave of Sedava]], gathered a mob of peasantry to march on the Duma in Novoanov, but was blocked by the Ledestrov military, firmly in the pockets of the Duma’s nobles. Under the [[Count of Litwaldov]], Sedava’s untrained mob was smashed at the [[Battle of Lisebev]], with Sedava himself captured. Sedava would be executed for treason, with the Count of Litwaldov crowned the new duke. Litwaldov would stamp out several smaller rebellions throughout his reign, but would only reign three years, succumbing to a heart attack in 1942. The Duma, paralyzed with corruption and infighting, could not manage a ⅔ majority. While normally the duke’s eldest child would be appointed regent, Litwaldov died childless. Faced with a succession crisis, a group of five nobles, headed by the [[Baron of Uzryta]], bribed the military leadership of Ledestrov to storm the Duma. All nobles who opposed Uzryta’s appointment as regent were imprisoned or executed, and many who remained would retreat to their estates after the appointment. Uzryta’s council, which would come to be known as the Pentarchy, forced many unpopular laws through the weakened Duma. While this led to rapid industrialization of Ledestrov, they did little to improve peoples’ lives. This, compounded with Uzryta’s refusal to allow the Duma to elect a new duke, as well as his perceived illegitimacy, would cause several mass strikes and protests across the duchy.

=== '''The Fall of the Pentarchy, and the Modern Duchy''' ===
After a decade of quashing demonstrations across the duchy, several members of the army began to join in the protests. Ever insecure about his position, [[Uzryta of Ledestrov|Uzryta]] forced a restructuring of the army through the Duma, and purged several senior officers. Growing frustrated with the Pentarchy, the head of the [[Southern Defense Force of Ledestrov|Southern Defense Force]], the [[Count of Reznikoff]], refused orders to put down a minor insurrection, instead incorporating the rebels into his own forces and marching on Novoanov. As Uzryta attempted to rally forces to his cause, several members of the [[Duma of Ledestrov|Duma]] tried to assassinate him, along with the rest of the [[Pentarchy of Ledestrov|Pentarchy]]. Uzryta managed to escape, but two of the five lay dead. While seeking protection from any remaining loyal soldiers or police, Uzryta was attacked by a mob of angry citizens, and killed. Soon after, Reznikoff entered Novoanov, and was welcomed by the people as a savior from the anarchy engulfing the city. [[Reznikoff of Ledestrov|Reznikoff]] declared himself the duke, oversaw the execution of the remaining members of the Pentarchy, and began major reforms of the governing structure of the duchy. The Duma was expanded, adding several new members (appointed from Reznikoff’s loyalists in the military), as well as a lower house, with members popularly elected. He also established the eradication of corruption as an explicit duty of the duke, and personally oversaw the trials of many members of the Duma. Once the Duma had been stabilized, Reznikoff moved onto the military. While Uzryta’s reforms had been unpopular, Rezikoff’s history with the military allowed him to implement similar reforms with less opposition, bringing the military up to date, and on par with most of Ledestrov’s neighbors. As of the year 2003, Reznikoff, now in his early eighties, has begun to reform the economy, this time with a mind for the peoples’ wellbeing. Many worry that the so-called “Great Reformer” will soon be on death’s doorstep. Others worry for the future after his death. As Reznikoff was never elected by the Duma, many worry the duke’s heir, the young Countess of Anavaisk and Reznikoff’s granddaughter, will seize power on his death. The duke is even believed to support this outcome, having funded the construction of and taking up residence in Reznikoff Palace, in the old, pre-Accords capital of Anavaisk. While many in the 141 strong upper house of the Duma have voiced their opposition to this future, the 315 strong, popularly elected lower house has supported Reznikoff since its formation, and would likely see little opposition to the return of a hereditary monarchy should the Duma retain its power.

== Economic Structure ==
The economy of Ledestrov has undergone significant transformations, particularly under the reign of the "Great Reformer," Duke Reznikoff. The foundation of the economy is a blend of industrial and agricultural sectors, with a strong emphasis on self-sufficiency and state-led development.

Ledestrov boasts a robust heavy industrial base, focused on steel production, machinery, and armaments. This sector received a substantial boost during the Pentarchy, albeit at the cost of widespread discontent among the populace. Textile manufacturing and consumer goods production are also key components, employing a significant portion of the urban population. Many large industries remain under state control, ensuring that profits are reinvested into national development projects.

Agriculture in Ledestrov is organized around large collective farms, a legacy of historical reforms aimed at increasing productivity and ensuring food security. Recent efforts under Duke Reznikoff have aimed at modernizing agricultural practices, introducing mechanization, and improving crop yields.

Ledestrov’s economic policies prioritize the domestic market, encouraging local consumption and production. While not isolationist, Ledestrov maintains a cautious approach to foreign trade, favoring bilateral agreements that benefit national interests.

== Political Structure ==
Ledestrov’s political system is a constitutional duchy with a dual-chamber legislative body known as the Duma. The Duma is split into an upper house of landed nobles and a lower house of popularly elected representatives.

The Duke holds significant executive power, including the ability to propose laws, oversee the military, and conduct foreign relations. Duke Reznikoff's reforms have also emphasized anti-corruption measures and economic modernization.

The upper house of the Duma comprises 141 members, consisting of landed nobles who owe their allegiance to the Duke. This body is responsible for major decisions such as declarations of war, budgetary changes, and treaty approvals, requiring a simple majority for most decisions and a two-thirds majority for the election of a new Duke. The lower house, with 315 members elected by popular vote, serves as a check on the upper house, representing the interests of the broader populace and supporting many of Reznikoff’s reforms.

A rising political ideology within the Duma is [[Orderism]], which advocates for a more structured and hierarchical society. This revisionist faction is gradually gaining influence, particularly among those who view the current system as too chaotic and ineffective.

== Social Structure ==
The social structure of Ledestrov is characterized by a mix of traditional hierarchy and emerging authoritarian tendencies, with strong support for the Duke and his reforms.

The upper echelons of society consist of the landed nobles who play a crucial role in governance and own vast estates. Their power, however, has been curbed by Duke Reznikoff’s anti-corruption measures. Recent reforms have seen the rise of a new nobility, often military leaders or industrial magnates loyal to the Duke.

A growing middle class of bureaucrats, professionals, and small business owners supports the administration and benefits from the Duke’s reforms. Military officers hold a respected position in society, given the military’s central role in both governance and national stability.

The backbone of Ledestrov’s economy, industrial workers often live in urban centers and are subject to strict labor regulations. In rural areas, the peasantry works on collective farms. While their living conditions have improved under Reznikoff’s modernization efforts, they remain at the lower end of the social hierarchy.

There is a significant undercurrent of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalism nationalism] and [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Authoritarianism authoritarianism], with many in society supporting strong, centralized control and the Duke’s leadership. Policies often aim at creating a unified national identity, sometimes at the expense of individual freedoms and minority rights.

== Foreign Relations ==
Ledestrov’s foreign policy is pragmatic and focused on maintaining sovereignty and national interests. Ledestrov maintains cautious but generally peaceful relations with neighboring states, often using diplomacy to avoid conflict and secure beneficial trade agreements. Ledestrov prefers a non-aligned stance in global politics, avoiding entanglement in major power blocs while leveraging its position to gain economic and military aid. The duchy engages selectively in AGGPI. Ledestrov favors bilateral trade agreements that ensure mutual benefits and allow for the exchange of technology and resources. The duchy is open to receiving economic aid and investment, particularly for infrastructure projects that align with national development goals.
